_comment: design.md section 12's fixture corpus: (message, senderHint, expectedVerdict, expectedEvidenceTypes), run against the real Phase 1 pipeline (MessageNormalizer + the three rule analyzers + FusionPolicy) with the classifier permanently absent, exactly as :app ships it. Loaded and asserted by VerdictFixtureTest.kt. expectedEvidenceTypes is a subset check (evidence the fixture must contain, not an exhaustive list); expectedAbsentEvidenceTypes is the inverse, for exemption cases.
_comment_verdicts: Many wording-only fixtures below (no URL/sender trigger) expect SAFE even though the message is obviously scam-flavored to a human. This is verified, correct Phase 1 behavior, not an undertuned test: the pattern analyzer's own fusion weight is only 0.08 (design.md section 7 step 2), capped at 0.5 internally, so even a maximally-matched pattern-only message renormalizes (classifier absent) to about 0.09 -- deep in the SAFE band (< 0.35). Only the URL and sender analyzers (weights 0.25 / 0.12, and the only two allowed to set forceVerdict) can move a Phase 1 verdict out of SAFE. This is the direct, intended consequence of design.md's own words: 'rules alone must not produce a confident SCAM on wording evidence' -- it is simply a stronger floor than 'not SCAM' alone. Fixing this requires the classifier (Phase 4), not a rule change.
